episode_summary: Litecoin podcast-style episode TBP126 (2017-05-01) interviews Litecoin creator Charlie Lee about Litecoin's SegWit activation through miner signaling. Covers why miners and pools resisted, the F2Pool signaling turn, the price moving in step with signaling, user-activated soft fork fallback, Lightning and confidential transactions on Litecoin, Coinbase's Token wallet, and a host segment on the Antminer call-home switch.

cards.claim: In May 2017 the hosts explained that Litecoin was designed to resist ASICs so people could mine it on GPUs.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Litecoin was created to try and keep people from having specialized hardware so they can do it on GPUs and so on and so forth

cards.claim: In May 2017 the hosts said the Lightning Network had already worked on the Litecoin testnet.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the lightning network already worked on the Litecoin test net it works flawlessly

cards.claim: In May 2017 Litecoin was trading around $14.80 on Coinbase, down from $16.11 earlier.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's at 14.80, according to Coinbase. 14.80 is not bad. It was at 16.11.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee argued that SegWit was sold as a scaling solution, so people only saw it as that and missed its other benefits.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: Segwit was sold as a scaling solution in the Bitcoin space. And unfortunately, that caused people to only see it as a scaling solution.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said SegWit enables Lightning and confidential transactions, not just scaling.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: in reality Segwit allows us to do like lightning networks to do a lot of other things with software like confidential transactions

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said Litecoin would complement Bitcoin as a payment network for smaller everyday purchases.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: I see Litecoin as always complementing Bitcoin to be more of a form of payment for buying smaller things

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said Litecoin had four times Bitcoin's throughput because its blocks arrive every two and a half minutes.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: But off the get-go, we have four times the capacity of Bitcoin

cards.claim: Charlie Lee predicted Litecoin would have many years before it ran into scaling problems.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: And if we do, I think we'll have many years to go before we actually run into any scaling issues.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said most miners are driven by cash flow rather than ideology and do not understand the protocol.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: They're not driven by ideology. They're driven by the cash flow that they're printing.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said SegWit on Litecoin would activate if the five or six big mining pools started signaling for it.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: so it mostly comes down to like the five or six big pools if we manage to convince um the pools to start signaling to support segwit then it'll activate

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said he persuaded an individual miner with about 10% of global hashrate to signal for SegWit on Litecoin.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: So I talked to an individual miner who had like 10% of the global hash rate, a pretty big miner.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said F2Pool started signaling for SegWit on Litecoin after its owner was persuaded.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: f2 pool after talking to him for a while um the the owner decided to

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said the Litecoin price moved in lockstep with the SegWit signaling percentage after F2Pool began signaling.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: from that point onwards, the price of Litecoin was in lockstep with the signaling percentage.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee described a user-activated soft fork, where exchanges and wallets enforce activation after a set period if users want it.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: So the idea was the user-activated software. Basically, if users all want it and exchanges serve the users

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said SegWit is an opt-in soft fork, so users who do not want SegWit transactions do not have to use them.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: Because SegWit is a soft fork and it's opt-in. If you don't want to use SegWit transactions, you don't have to.

cards.claim: In May 2017 Charlie Lee said he was never in doubt that SegWit would activate on Litecoin, whether by miner or user activation.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: So I was never really in doubt that SegWit would activate on Litecoin.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee explained BIP 9 miner activation: after code release, miners upgrade over months until about 95 percent signal, then the soft fork locks in.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: So eventually, 95% of miners or pools have all upgraded. And once they've upgraded, then you can lock in the soft fork.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said the team hoped to have Lightning Network working on Litecoin by the time SegWit activated, about two weeks later.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: and hopefully we'll have something actually working by the time Segwit activates in two weeks

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said confidential transactions could be added to Litecoin as a soft fork once SegWit was in place.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: So with Segwit, confidential transactions can be done as a soft fork and that's exciting.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said speculation is currently the main killer app for Bitcoin and Litecoin.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: Right now, it's kind of just like mostly on trading, right? Speculation is the killer app.

cards.claim: Charlie Lee said Coinbase was working on Token, its Ethereum wallet, as a product the company was exploring.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: we have a team working on a product called Token, which is our Ethereum wallet

cards.claim: Charlie Lee gave a ten-word definition of Bitcoin as an electronic currency not backed by government.
cards.speaker: Charlie Lee
cards.quote: so bitcoin is a electronic currency that is not backed by government

cards.claim: In May 2017 the host predicted the ICO space might implode because too much money was chasing speculative projects.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i think the the whole icl space is is kind of scary to me i think it might kind of implode

cards.claim: The hosts said the Antminer S9 included an undocumented call-home function that checked in every 1 to 11 minutes and could shut miners off.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Every 1 to 11 minutes, it sends a signal back to AntMiner servers to essentially verify that it's mining.

cards.claim: The hosts said the fix for the Antminer call-home issue sat in GitHub for seven months without being implemented.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the fix for this sat in GitHub for seven months and just wasn't ever implemented

cards.claim: The host said the SegWit experiment on Litecoin would give Bitcoin developers real-world confidence to deploy the same technology on Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: we now have an experiment, a side experiment, to test everything that we've been creating in Bitcoin

title: TBP126 - Litecoin's SegWit Activation
